# The Hard Truth {background-color="#332288" background-image="https://www.transparenttextures.com/patterns/asfalt-dark.png"}

## The Iron Rule of Scientific Software Development

::: {.problem-card .fragment}
### The Efficiency Trap
"If you take the time to build out code the right way, you will never use it."
:::

::: {.problem-card .fragment}
### The Technical Debt
"If you write sloppy code, it will bite you in the ass."
:::

::: {.solution-card .fragment}
### The Equilibrium
**Damned if you do. Damned if you don't.** Unless you automate the structure itself.
:::

## The Python Paradox {auto-animate=true}

::: {.problem-card .fragment}
- Python is a **TERRIBLE** language for scientific computing.
- Nothing about the language is inherently good for science.
- Most tools were developed by researchers as a "side-hustle."
:::

# The Circle

```{python}
#| echo: false
#| fig-align: center
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

with plt.xkcd():
    fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(10, 6))
    
    # Venn circles
    c1 = plt.Circle((0.4, 0.5), 0.35, fc='none', ec='black', lw=2)
    c2 = plt.Circle((0.6, 0.5), 0.35, fc='none', ec='black', lw=2)
    ax.add_patch(c1)
    ax.add_patch(c2)

    # Annotations
    ax.annotate("THINGS I HATE WITH\nA VISCERAL PASSION", 
                xy=(0.25, 0.5), xytext=(0.05, 0.85),
                arrowprops=dict(arrowstyle='->', connectionstyle="arc3,rad=.2"))
    
    ax.annotate("STANDARD SCIENTIFIC\nCOMPUTING WORKFLOWS", 
                xy=(0.75, 0.5), xytext=(0.95, 0.85),
                ha='right', arrowprops=dict(arrowstyle='->', connectionstyle="arc3,rad=-.2"))

    # The intersection items
    items = ["JUPYTER", "SLURM", "CONDA", "MATPLOTLIB"]
    ax.text(0.5, 0.5, "\n".join(items), ha='center', va='center', 
            fontsize=14, fontweight='bold')

    ax.set_xlim(0, 1)
    ax.set_ylim(0, 1)
    ax.axis('off')
    plt.show()
```

# The Good News {background-color="#AA4499"}

:::

# Tools of the Trade {background-color="#332288"}

## 1. VSCode / Cursor {auto-animate=true}

::::: columns
::: {.column width="50%"}
::: {.problem-card .fragment}
### Anti-Pattern
**Stop using Jupyter Notebooks for everything.** Notebooks are for **exploration**, not **logic**.
:::
:::

::: {.column width="50%"}
::: {.solution-card .fragment}
### Modern IDE
Localize your logic. Use **Cursor** for AI-native pair programming to move 10x faster.
:::
:::
:::::

::: footer
Doc: [code.visualstudio.com](https://code.visualstudio.com) \| [cursor.com](https://www.cursor.com)
:::

## 2. Project Structure {auto-animate=true}

::::: columns
::: {.column width="50%"}
::: {.problem-card .fragment}
### The Mess
Separate source code from sweeps. Don't drown in a directory of `.ipynb` files.
:::
:::

::: {.column width="50%"}
::: {.solution-card .fragment}
### Modularity
Make your code a **module**. Modular code is **testable** code.
:::
:::
:::::

::: footer
Doc: [git-scm.com](https://git-scm.com)
:::

## 3. UV: The New Standard {auto-animate=true}

::::: columns
::: {.column width="48%"}
::: {.problem-card .fragment}
### Environment Hell
"It works on my machine, but the cluster environment is broken."
:::
:::

::: {.column width="48%"}
::: {.solution-card .fragment}
### The Solution
**UV**: Reproducible environments with `uv.lock`. Byte-for-byte consistency across all machines.
:::
:::
:::::

::: footer
Doc: [docs.astral.sh/uv](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/)
:::

## 4. Pydantic: Strong Typing {auto-animate=true}

::::: columns
::: {.column width="48%"}
::: {.problem-card .fragment}
### Loose Data
Constantly parsing nested lists/dicts and hitting silent runtime bugs.
:::
:::

::: {.column width="48%"}
::: {.solution-card .fragment}
### The Solution
**Validation**: Catch errors at the boundary. Give your LLM a precise schema to work with.
:::
:::
:::::

::: footer
Doc: [docs.pydantic.dev](https://docs.pydantic.dev/)
:::

## 5. Snakemake: Orchestration {auto-animate=true}

::::: columns
::: {.column width="48%"}
::: {.problem-card .fragment}
### Pipeline Amnesia
"How did I generate this figure? What results are stale?"
:::
:::

::: {.column width="48%"}
::: {.solution-card .fragment}
### The Solution
**DAG Generation**: Snakemake knows exactly what needs to run. The script *is* the record.
:::
:::
:::::

::: footer
Doc: [snakemake.github.io](https://snakemake.github.io/)
:::
